rows.note: INFERRED: the 64 um mask of the sky and calibration fibers is the width the science slices share ('the same slit width'). Three slices of 64 um use 192 um of the 225 um octagon, and the leftover outer edges go to the exposure meter, as the paper says. The papers do not state the science slice width as a number. At the f/8 slit this is 64 x 8/3.7 = 138 um (DERIVED, assuming the magnification between the fiber and the slit follows the ratio of the focal ratios); on sky, 64 um / (3.7 x 10.95 m) = 0.326 arcsec.

sources.quote: Through this combination of slicing and masking, all of the orderlets feature the same “slit” width in the spectral direction

rows.note: DERIVED: slit width at the f/8 collimator focus 138 um, so the explorer's slit angle is 138 um / (8 x 10.95 m) = 0.326 arcsec (= 64 um / (3.7 x 10.95 m)). Slit-limited geometric R = 2 tan(theta_B) f_col / w = 2 x 3.9989 x 1600 mm / 0.1384 mm = 92,500 (rectangular top-hat), against the measured 95,000-97,000. The slicing makes the line profile a top-hat convolved with the camera PSF, which the explorer's Rs row will show as a ~5% miss; a miss, not tuned away.

rows.value: xd 'vph', xGlass silica; physical 810 and 450 /mm; start the explorer's effective xG at 648 (green) and 360 (red) and refit to the order counts

sources.quote: The monochromatic beam diameter here is 160 mm

rows.note: EFFECTIVE (to be refit by the preset builder): the explorer's camera focal length is the effective one in echelle angle space (618.75 mm, row cam_eff), but the VPH acts on the real 160 mm beam and the real 495 mm camera, so the grating line density seen by the explorer's angles is scaled by 495/618.75 = 0.8: 648 /mm (green), 360 /mm (red). The order spacing check, DERIVED with the physical numbers: order m at 520 nm is 118 (m lambda_B = 2 d sin theta_B = 61.40 um); the free spectral range is 4.4 nm, the angular dispersion of an 810 /mm grating gives 1.766 mm = 118 px between orders on a 495 mm camera, and 35 orders x 118 px = 4120 px, against the 4080 px chip; red (450 /mm, 735 nm, m = 84.5, 492 mm): 125 px x 32 orders = 3990 px. So the physical grating numbers reproduce the published order counts to 1-3 percent.
